arguments.content:
MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF MOTION FOR SUMMARY JUDGMENT

I. Introduction
This Memorandum supports Defendant Upjohn Co.'s Motion for Summary Judgment. Based on the record, no genuine issue of material fact exists, and Defendant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law under Fed. R. Civ. P. 56.

II. Legal Standard
Under Celotex Corp. v. Catrett, 477 U.S. 317 (1986), the moving party need not negate the opponent’s claim but must demonstrate the absence of a genuine issue of material fact. Anderson v. Liberty Lobby, Inc., 477 U.S. 242 (1986) requires the court to view evidence in the light most favorable to the non-moving party.

III. Application
Plaintiff has failed to produce evidence sufficient to support a finding in its favor on the essential elements of its claim. The depositions, affidavits, and internal memoranda demonstrate uniformity of corporate policy and lack of discriminatory intent.

IV. Conclusion
Defendant respectfully requests the Court grant summary judgment.

Respectfully submitted,
[Attorney Name]
Covington & Burling
